grades.quote: Programs that exhibit strong locality of reference will perform much better, not only because of the cache hierarchy, but also because of the TLB. The performance drop-off when your program exceeds the TLB’s capacity is generally quite precipitous.
grades.reason: Directly identifies TLB capacity and poor locality as reasons for sharp slowdowns, applicable when page-sized strides touch many distinct pages.

grades.quote: In order for the system’s performance not to fall off sharply on larger workloads, the TLB must be reasonably large (perhaps hundreds of entries), so that it can still prevent most page table accesses.
grades.reason: Explains limited translation caching and the additional page-table accesses on misses, providing a substantive explanation for slow page-strided array access.

grades.quote: Also, if page table references exhibit spatial locality, keeping at least a small cluster of consecutive pages’ entries adjacent could speed access.
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary information about locality in translation lookups, but does not explain page-strided array slowdowns or TLB capacity.
Discusses disk seeks, rotational latency, and sector locality rather than memory-page-strided array access.
